Printing press

Machine used to transfer ink to a surface

A printing press brings a prepared printing surface into contact with material such as paper. Different mechanisms serve the same basic purpose.

Diagram placeholder for a historical machine.

Historyedit

Main subject: History of printing.

Reusable type, ink, paper, and pressure came together in systems that enabled repeated impressions. Later machinery increased the speed of production.

Mechanism

Type
Reusable pieces form the printing surface.
Pressure
A mechanism transfers the ink evenly.

Illustrative quotation: careful preparation makes repeated impressions consistent.

Fixture commentary

Impact

More copies could circulate among readers, encouraging new patterns of publication and distribution.
